author_explanation: 'if no answer is provided, the program will pick one'.
Life events concentrate on 'marriages, divorces, the births of children, and deaths'; 'Other parts of the program allow other sorts of history to be added.'
The user 'let the program pick her name (Kathy Cole)'.
Result: 'a swinging sleazy doctor and taxidriver'.
The essay glosses niceness 3 / self-confidence 4 / intelligence 3 as 'not very nice … moderately self-confident, and moderately intelligent' (see Q-CHAR-3).
test_expectations: A create-to-specification run with targets {niceness 3, self-confidence 4, intelligence 3} first picks one occupation by minimal discrepancy.
Traits already matched by the occupation are reported satisfied and skipped.
For each remaining trait, candidate stereotypes are those that do not alter already-set values and move the trait toward its target.

Exact candidate sets (sleazy-doctor; life-guard/swinger/big-eater; taxidriver) are reproducible ONLY with the original stereotype library, which is lost; the reconstruction can reproduce the procedure, not these lists.
